title: How the Gillette pro-Palestine suppression narrative changed
summary: Tracks Owens’s account of Kraft excluding Macklemore and her later presentation of Zach Bryan’s same-stadium pro-Palestine performances as a response. It records the evolution of her suppression-versus-defiance narrative, without establishing venue policy, motives or attendance figures.

milestones.label: Macklemore exclusion alleged
milestones.proposition: Owens alleges that Kraft used pressure to cancel Macklemore as Sheeran’s opening act after pro-Palestine remarks, presenting the stadium as an example of powerful actors suppressing that speech.
milestones.review_note: Reviewed the earlier source’s 2710–2909s context and canonical statement appearance at 2794.26; its publication date is September 15, not a dated ban occurrence. The compound canonical statement excerpt spans the pressure and eventual-success account. No ban notice, contractual authority or motive is independently authenticated. The current source repeats this same canonical accusation at 2703.44 rather than supplying a second distinct ban milestone.
milestones.statement_text: Owens said Robert Kraft, the billionaire owner of the New England Patriots and their stadium, mounted a pressure campaign that succeeded in having Macklemore canceled as Ed Sheeran's opening act.

milestones.label: Stadium defiance celebrated
milestones.proposition: Owens presents Zach Bryan and his band wearing Free Palestine shirts at the same stadium, with a claimed attendance record, as a response showing that the suppression she attributed to Kraft is failing.
milestones.review_note: Reviewed 2665–2838s, including the source’s explicit recall of Macklemore’s exclusion and perfect-response wording at 2748s. This is a reviewed evolution of the same venue suppression narrative, not a link inferred from shared artists or Palestine. The performances and record are attributed to Owens; no attendance figure, coordinated intention, rescission of the earlier ban or causal relationship is independently established. The drummer and unidentified child are incidental details, not milestone participants.
milestones.statement_text: Owens said Zach Bryan and his entire band wore Free Palestine shirts at Gillette Stadium, that Bryan wore one on both nights, and that he broke the stadium attendance record previously held by Ed Sheeran on the second night.
milestones.speaker: Candace Owens

links.review_note: Prior statement-11a85be217aa alleged successful suppression at Kraft’s stadium. Current statement-1b39318d5161 is explicitly framed at 2665–2838s as the same stadium’s response and a challenge to that power. This expands the narrative from exclusion to alleged public defiance; it does not refute the earlier exclusion, prove that Zach intended a response or verify record attendance.
